project.title: MMS 172 Assignment 2 - Simulated News Broadcast (Group 36)
project.description: My group and I created a simulated radio news broadcast for our MMS 172 project. We recorded our parts at home and then combined all the files in REAPER. I was in charge of arranging the nine tracks, using ReaComp, and creating sidechain ducking effects for the mixing board. Among the problems we encountered while preparing the project, one of them was related to the fact that we had to work with files recorded in different places with different equipment. Furthermore, we encountered unexpected situations, including stormy weather and floods, that impacted our work. Finally, we managed to create an eight-minute and forty-three-second long radio news broadcast and exported the file in stereo WAV format.

project.title: Photography: Bucketlist
project.description: For my MMS 173 Photography Project, I was able to take five shots of my own using my Sony A6400 camera around Sipalay City. I captured one photo per theme which are location, pattern, silhouette, night, and motion, and included each in my project. One picture was taken at the beach while the sun set, one was a pattern of archways, one was my friend sitting at the front of a formation of rocks, one was the city hall at night, and the last was the cascade at Baclao. In addition to the photographs, I described in the assignment how I framed my shots and adjusted my camera's settings based on the location. I wrote about the shots I took and what I observed when taking them, as well as the points I wanted to convey with each one.

project.title: What I Kept
project.description: What I Kept refers to the title of my final project for MMS 173. I selected ten photos for my portfolio, including those captured in my experience with Lushfoil Photography Sim, and some from the places and moments that I encountered during my life. Specifically, I captured scenes at Sugar Beach, a photo with my dog Yumi at our front door and moments from my closest friend's wedding that continued until the early morning. For each photo, I described what attracted my attention and how I captured it, including the camera settings. Some photos were planned, while others were captured by chance when I noticed something that wanted to be captured by my camera.
